claim: One failed SendGrid cancel aborts the whole cancellation loop and discards every queued row delete, so the same failing reminder blocks all later cancellations on every cron run and those emails are sent.

Rescheduling (and workflow/step deletion) still cancel at SendGrid immediately via immediateDelete=true, which hits the same 100-pending-cancellation cap the PR describes, so reminders for rescheduled bookings are still sent once the cap is reached.
body:
## [ISSUE] Rescheduling still uses the immediate SendGrid cancel that hits the 100-pending cap

**Severity:** HIGH - issue #7225 (emails still sent for rescheduled bookings) is not fixed for the most common reschedule path.

### The Problem

```ts
originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => {
  if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) {
    deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true);
```

When `immediateDelete === true`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` (`emailReminderManager.ts:213-222`) sends `POST /v3/user/scheduled_sends {status: "cancel"}` straight away. It does not set `cancelled: true` and let the cron cancel later.

### Theory / Proof

The PR description gives the root cause: SendGrid keeps every cancelled batch in `scheduled_sends` until its send time, and accepts at most 100 pending cancellations. Once there are 100, new cancel requests fail and the emails are sent anyway. The fix is to hold cancellations back until the send time is less than 1 hour away, so the number pending at any moment stays small.

`handleNewBooking` runs for every attendee or host reschedule. Emails are scheduled at SendGrid up to 72 hours ahead (`scheduleEmailReminders.ts:85`). Every reschedule therefore adds a cancellation that stays pending for up to 72 hours, which is the same pattern that caused the original failure. The error is caught at `emailReminderManager.ts:233` and only logged. The surrounding `try/catch` (lines 964-975) cannot catch it anyway, because the async calls are not awaited.

The same `true` flag is passed in `workflows.tsx` (workflow delete, around line 213, and step delete, around line 521). Deleting one workflow that is active on busy event types can create more than 100 cancellations at once.

### What happens today vs. what will break

With low volume the immediate cancel works. At production volume the 100 cap is reached again and reminders for rescheduled bookings go out. This is exactly what the PR sets out to fix.

### Research

SendGrid's "Cancel Scheduled Sends" docs state the limit: "You can have up to 100 pending cancellations or pauses at any one time". Cal.com's own analysis in this PR description relies on that limit.

### Recommendation

Use the deferred path for reschedules, the same way `handleCancelBooking` and `requestReschedule` in `bookings.tsx` now do. The reminder rows belong to the old booking, which is not deleted, so the cron will still find them:

```ts
if (reminder.method === WorkflowMethods.EMAIL) {
  deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId);
}
```

Workflow and step deletion only need the immediate path because `onDelete: Cascade` removes the rows. For those, consider keeping the rows (for example, detach them or soft-delete the step) so the cron can handle them too. The alternative is to keep immediate cancellation but add a comment that it counts against the cap.

claim: The immediateDelete branch cancels at SendGrid but leaves the row (and any existing cancelled=true flag) in place, so a reminder already flagged by requestReschedule is cancelled twice and the cron's second cancel fails.

The reminder cancellation DB writes are no longer awaited (previously they were part of the awaited Promise.all), so in a serverless function they may never run after the response is returned and the reminder is never flagged or deleted.
